title: Delegated Redaction Proxy and Retention Harden for Cross-Tenant Traces
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce a Delegated Redaction Proxy (DRP) that sits in the observability ingest path to enforce tenant-scoped PII redaction rules, apply tiered retention compaction, and emit immutable access logs for just-in-time reveal requests. The DRP will integrate with existing tracing hooks and metrics/log pipelines and provide a pluggable policy engine for platform and customer policies.
acceptance_criteria: DRP deployed in canary region and accepts trace/metric/log events without schema changes
Tenant policy lookup implemented and applied within 50ms of ingest for 99% of requests
PII fields defined by policy are redacted or pseudonymized before durable storage
Tiered retention compaction runs and compresses traces older than TTL thresholds without data loss for current SLOs
Access log shows every unmask/unblind event with actor, justification, and PR number if used for debugging
RBAC controls allow temporary reveal with auto-expiry and require security_review_required flag for sensitive tenants
Latency impact on tail p95 for ingest pipeline is < 15% in canary compared to baseline
implementation_notes: Use sidecar DRP service deployed in the observability ingest fleet; avoid changing producer clients
Policy engine: reuse existing tenant metadata store; cache policies in-memory with TTL and invalidation hooks
Redaction modes: strip, mask (salted hash), pseudonymize (reversible with HSM escrow), and annotate-with-token
Just-in-time reveal requires an escrow workflow: request -> approval step (security or cust-owned) -> short-lived key unwrap via HSM -> audit entry
Retention: implement compaction job that converts high-cardinality trace spans into summarized artifacts for long-term storage
Integrate with console dashboards: show per-tenant redaction rates, retention compaction savings, and reveal audit metrics
Telemetry: emit internal metrics for policy-evaluation-latency, redaction-rate, reveal-request-rate, and compaction-throughput
design_decisions: Architectural choice: sidecar/delegated proxy vs in-producer SDK — chose DRP to avoid forced client changes and centralize policy enforcement
Storage strategy: keep compacted summaries for >30d retention to balance cost vs debugability
Reveal model: reversible unmasking gated by HSM-backed keys to meet compliance for regulated customers
RBAC model: use role-bound temporary tokens issued by Console with automatic expiry and recorded justification
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: DRP introduces a latency hop that could affect p95/p99 — Mitigation: async evaluation for non-blocking rules and local caching of policies
Risk: Key management for reversible pseudonymization adds complexity — Mitigation: integrate with existing KMS/HSM and create a limited-scope escrow service with strict audit logging
Risk: Policy drift across regions — Mitigation: put policy versioning and canary gating into rollout pipeline
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): prefer conservative default policies per tenant and explicit opt-in for reversible pseudonymization
Security (Ravi Patel): require offline attestation for any reveal and log export to WORM storage for compliance customers
Design (Maya Chen): request a visual flow for DRP in the Confluence design doc before wide rollout
Infra (Diego Ramos): suggest CPU profiling in canary; prefer Rust service for predictable latencies
